messages.subject: writing customized nimbleFunction
parts:
1. I would like to write my own nimbleFunction, but I always get some errors that I have no idea how to fix it. According to the user manual version 0.5-1, "Run code is provided in the NIMBLE language. This is similar to a narrow subset of R, but it is important to remember that it is different -....". My question is which subset of R (language) can be used in NIMBLE language, and what kind of rules that I need to follow in order to compile my customized nimble function. If I can run the uncompiled customized nimbleFunction, can I also run the compiled nimbleFunction?

2. Does nimble support sparse matrix like sparse matrix in Matrix, spam package?

Hi Perry,

Thanks for your reply.

I did read the user manual, and what bothers me is that I cannot find a clear-cut between what Nimble can do and what it cannot do with some features or functionalities in R. For example, in the user manual 0.5-1, Table 5.4 and 5.5 indicate whether some operations and functions (defined or used) in R are currently supported in Nimble, and I know from these tables that I cannot use some R functions in Nimble, but what about other R functions: Bessel functions (BesselI(...), BesselK(...), etc.), diagonal function (diag(...)), kronecker product (kronecker(...)), and many others? Are they supported in Nimble currently?

Just another minor concern about the variable type, it seems that currently Nimble supports double, integer, character, logical, and void. Will nimble support some other types like list in R or cell array in Matlab, or field in Matlab in the near future? Since it's painful to define too many arguments in many nimbleFunctions.

I attached one of my own nimbleFunction, and I cannot compile it due to some errors see below. More importantly, I cannot find any clue to fix these errors by my own. It would be nice if future release of Nimble will provide more detailed debug features so that the nimble users can fix their own errors most of the time.

The error message is:

Error in match(x, table, nomatch = 0L) : 
  'match' requires vector arguments
Error: There is some problem at the setSizes processing step for this code:

The test code is 
## test woodbury
n <- 10
r <- 3
C <- exp(-as.matrix(dist(rnorm(r)))/0.5)
A <- diag(rgamma(n, 5, 2))
U <- matrix(rgamma(n*r, 3, 2), n, r)
V <- t(U)
p <- 1
T <- as.matrix(rnorm(n*p), n, p)

sol <- woodbury(A, U, C, V, T)

Cwoodbury <- compileNimble(woodbury)
Csol <- Cwoodbury(A, U, C, V, T)


BWT, I really like to work with Nimble to do computation in my research and I hope Nimble would become better as time goes.

Thank you very much!

Pulong

messages.author: dd632bd3bbcdd7e9
messages.subject: Re: writing customized nimbleFunction
parts:
Hi Pulong,

Thanks for your feedback.  We will try to add something to the manual to make clearer what is supported.  In the meantime, a good guideline is that if something is not explained in the manual, then it is not included.  We have a lot of plans to extend nimble to include more, and if you’re interested in contributing to development we’d be happy to help you implement some of those things.  There are a lot of competing priorities for very limited developer time and we’d be really delighted to have new contributors.

Regarding types: again what is available is in the manual.  I understand you have found it hard to get a summary of what’s available in the manual, but it’s the best resource I can point you to right now.  No, there is not support for R lists or matlab-type features.  Section 9.5.19 shows how you can create a user-defined data structure, which at the moment is nothing more than a trick of writing a nimbleFunction with setup code but no run code.

Another resource is our github wiki: https://github.com/nimble-dev/nimble/wiki.  It’s not very complete but on the right column you’ll see a preliminary list of “What works in the DSL… “ (domain-specific language, i.e. nimbleFunction run code).

Here is a modified version of your woodbury function that successfully compiles.  The main issue was that we do not yet support diag().

woodbury <- nimbleFunction(
    run = function(A=double(2), U=double(2), C=double(2), V=double(2), 
        T=double(2)) {
        n <- dim(A)[1]
        AInv <- matrix(0, nrow = n, ncol = n)
        for(i in 1:n) AInv[i,i] <- 1/A[i,i]
        ##AInv <- diag(1/diag(A))
        nC <- dim(C)[1]
        Identity <- matrix(nrow = nC, ncol = nC) ## next version of nimble will have an identityMatrix function
        for(i in 1:nC) Identity[i,i] <- 1
        temp <- solve(C, Identity) + V%*%AInv%*%U
        ##temp <- solve(C, diag(rep(1,nimDim(C)[1]))) + V%*%AInv%*%U
        sol <- AInv%*%T - AInv%*%U%*%solve(temp, V%*%AInv%*%T)
        return(sol)
        returnType(double(2))
})

Please let us know further questions.  At this time of year our responses will be slower due to various travel by various nimble developers.

Best wishes
Perry

Minor correction, the currently released version v0.5-1 of the NIMBLE language DSL already does support the function identityMatrix(d), with R help entry:

> library(nimble)
> ?identityMatrix
Create an Identity matrix
Description:
     Returns a d-by-d identity matrix (square matrix of 0's, with 1's
     on the main diagnol).
Usage:
     identityMatrix(d)
Arguments:
       d: The size of the identity matrix to return, will return a
          d-by-d matrix
Details:
     This function can be used in the NIMBLE DSL, i.e. in the run
     function and member methods of nimbleFunctions.
Value:
     A d-by-d identity matrix
Author(s):
     Daniel Turek
Examples:
     Id <- identityMatrix(d = 3)

Hi Perry,

Thanks for pointing out such useful information, and thanks Daniel for pointing out the IdentityMatrix function.

I am planning to write some nimble codes to implement a Bayesian spatio-temporal statistical model for very large dataset (in order of 10^7) that I am currently working on, and would like to gain some speed-ups for MCMC algorithm. All the codes for the model have been written in MATLAB. What bothers me is that some of the calculation such as eigenvalues for the first largest one, sparse matrix computation have not been implemented yet in NIMBLE. 

I noticed that the fixed woodbury R code is slightly faster than the compiled one when I run it on Mac. Any explanation for this? Does nimble internally use different linear algebra library than R?

## test woodbury
n <- 10000 # or 1000
r <- 300

C <- exp(-as.matrix(dist(rnorm(r)))/0.5)
A <- diag(rgamma(n, 5, 2))
U <- matrix(rgamma(n*r, 3, 2), n, r)
V <- t(U)
p <- 1
T <- as.matrix(rnorm(n*p), n, p)
ts <- proc.time()
sol <- woodbury(A, U, C, V, T)

proc.time() - ts

Cwoodbury <- compileNimble(woodbury)
ts <- proc.time()
Csol <- Cwoodbury(A, U, C, V, T)

proc.time() - ts



Thanks,
Pulong

messages.author: 5fa2a363d4ddd1d1
messages.subject: Re: writing customized nimbleFunction
parts:
Hi Pulong,

Sparse matrix stuff is on our radar screen but not yet available.

R uses BLAS and LAPACK behind the scenes, so it's already fully
vectorized and using compiled code under the hood (particularly good
if you have a fast and threaded BLAS available). NIMBLE uses Eigen for
linear algebra (apart from basic density and simulation calculates
(e.g., dmnorm) for which it uses the same BLAS+LAPACK as R). So while
there may be some differences in speed I'd expect that NIMBLE won't
give much speedup relative to pure linear algebra calculations done
from R.

Also, you probably know this but the order of operations when you do
the matrix multiplies can matter for the Woodbury computation. You can
enforce an order using parentheses in NIMBLE run code as in R.

chris

Regarding the computation time comparisons you’ve made: I’ll add that currently there are extra copy and initialization operations involved in getting into and returning from a compiled nimbleFunction, and for a small computation that computational cost can be important. One aspect of this should be improved in our upcoming release of version 0.6, while another aspect remains on the to-do list.

Perry
